newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Colgate-Palmolive happy with Brazil ruling.
newsitem.headline: Colgate-Palmolive happy with Brazil ruling.

text.p: U.S. personal hygiene giant Colgate-Palmolive said Thursday it was satisfied with a ruling by Brazil's anti-trust watchdog allowing the takeover of Brazilian oral hygiene firm Anakol.

"We are satisfied with the approval of the investment we made in our most important business area, oral hygiene, in the biggest and most powerful economy of Latin America," administrative board president Reuben Mark said in a statement.

Brazil's Administrative Economic Defence Council (Cade) ruled late Wednesday in favor of the buyout, but set conditions to keep Colgate from snapping up a 77 percent market share of Brazil's toothpaste market overnight.
Colgate's Mark, speaking in New York but whose comments were distributed in Brasilia, said the firm would submit a business plan to Cade within the required time to meet the conditions.
He added that the Cade decision would not affect Colgate's plan to export the toothpaste brand Kolynos to other Latin American countries and emerging markets.

Cade gave Colgate three alternatives: refrain from selling the Kolynos brand for four years, license it to a third party over 20 years, or sell the brand to a competitor with a less than one percent market share.
"We believe we will reach an accord which meets the conditions of Cade," Mark said.
Kolynos accounts for about 50 percent of Brazilian toothpaste sales and gives Colgate a 77 percent market share.
Anakol makes Kolynos in several Latin American countries. The Brazil operation represents $760 million of the 1995 buyout.
